Root construction, synthesis, and executable contract
1 November 2026, Australia/Brisbane

What was strengthened
======================
MAIN_PROOF.txt first supplied the common stationary law and the target mass
and conditional sampler. The extension here earns those computational inputs
from local calibration for a restricted interacting model. It does not infer
an arbitrary physical mechanism. The pinned Astra N1213 acquisition ingredient
already learns local heatbath probabilities and compatible Ising weights;
this work credits and reuses that ingredient. The extension adds driven local
cycles, coarse targets, the joint weights/flows sensitivity proof, and the
screened mean and lifetime receiver. Standard inverse-Ising identification,
transfer matrices, Dobrushin coupling and potential theory remain its machinery.

An equally informed conventional method can adopt all these constructions.
No new universal feasibility class, strongest-method speed superiority or
historical priority has been established by this work.

1. A useful general sensitivity theorem
=======================================
Let L=-Q be a finite irreducible generator with positive unnormalized invariant
weights w. Write D=diag(w)L. The directed flows w(x)q_xy are balanced, so D has
zero row and column sums. Decompose this flow into positive directed cycle
coefficients c_j on a specified common cycle architecture. A cycle has length
at most ell. Its ordinary bilinear form B_j and energy E_j obey
   |B_j(f,h)| <= K sqrt(E_j(f) E_j(h)),   K=csc(pi/ell).
This follows from the Fourier modes of a cycle. Two- and three-cycles have
K=2/sqrt(3)<=7/6. This concerns STATIONARY-FLOW cycles; state-dependent accepted
moves need not themselves be permutation kernels.

Let the fitted model have weights what and coefficients chat_j, satisfying
   exp(-u) w <= what <= exp(u) w pointwise,
   exp(-v) c_j <= chat_j <= exp(v) c_j for every cycle.
For any nonempty proper target A, let M and Mhat be mean hitting times from
the respective stationary laws conditioned on B=A^c.

Thus
   |log(Mhat/M)| <= 3u+Kv.                               (G2)

so g is supported on A, pi(g)=1, and g>=1 on A (because Q t>=0 there).

VERDICT

No substantive implementation error was found in the local ratio fit, rational
path target mass, conditional initializer, native proposal laws, stationary
cycle flow, boundary estimator, uniformized killing or mean interval formulas.
The declared n=80, D=100000 and clipping ranges fit the integer arithmetic.
The reporting and downstream qualifications below should remain explicit.

1. CALIBRATION AND FACTOR UNCERTAINTY

The80 a_i ratios use current0/current1 rates at neighbors00. The79 b_i ratios
use the additional right-neighbor1 setting divided by the already measured
00 ratio. The79 alpha_i observations use cycle state00, where local v=1 and
the actual positive transition rate is exactly alpha_i. This totals397=5n-3
independent synthetic Poisson counts as stated.

All true positive rates exceed1/3. The bound

  2*(5n-3)*exp[-T eta^2/9]

therefore follows from the standard relative Poisson Chernoff inequality.
The code uses an exact rational lower enclosure of the exponential in its
denominator, so the reported failure probability is an upper enclosure.

Nearest-grid rounding after clipping has absolute error at most1/(2D)=5e-6.
For a,b>=.9 and alpha>=.5, the chosen log allowance2e-5 per rounded factor is
conservative. Clipping itself cannot increase log error because all true
parameters lie in the clipping intervals.

With t=eta/(1-eta), the code's

  u=(6n-4)t+(2n-1)*roundlog,
  v=u+t+roundlog

correctly bound global unnormalized-weight error and flow error respectively.
The local cycle has unnormalized circulation alpha_i*C(outside), so the alpha
log error is paid once. The heatbath harmonic conductance needs only u.

Provided the proved weighted-flow theorem is used, the exponent3u+(7/6)v is
valid: the three-cycle sector constant2/sqrt(3) is less than7/6, and positive
Dirichlet inverses account for the two RHS-weight factors and one normalizer.
The exact rational exponential upper enclosure correctly certifies the chosen
5/4 model factor. This is a bound for true M versus fitted M; it is not a claim
that fitted pi equals true pi.
